opportunities.title: APEX Awards
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established independent researchers with a strong track record and proven ability to lead collaborative work; hold a permanent or fixed-term position covering the duration of the award; have teaching and admin duties from which they can be relieved; based in a UK University or UK not-for-profit research organisation. Up to two Co-applicants with complementary expertise covering a different Academy remit.
opportunities.summary: Cross-disciplinary research scheme (in partnership with the Royal Society and Royal Academy of Engineering, supported by the Leverhulme Trust) offering established independent researchers the opportunity to pursue genuine interdisciplinary, blue-skies, curiosity-driven research at the boundary between science, engineering and the social sciences/humanities.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to any researcher based in the UK who meets the conditions of the call; no prior British Academy funding required; previous successful recipients of this award are not eligible to reapply.
opportunities.summary: Public engagement programme supporting ambitious projects to engage the public with the humanities and social sciences, working in partnership with a gallery, archive, library or museum (GLAM organisation) or a performing arts organisation.

opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships

amount.raw: FEC regime; Academy funds 80 per cent of salary costs, directly allocated and indirect costs under FEC

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or recognised research organisation. British citizens and EEA nationals are eligible regardless of where the doctorate was obtained; anyone with a doctorate from a UK university of any nationality; or those demonstrating strong prior association with the UK. Viva Voce completed between 1 April 2024 and 1 April 2027. No permanent academic post held.
opportunities.summary: Three-year fellowships for outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences to pursue an independent research project towards completion of a significant piece of publishable research, funded by DSIT.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established researchers in the humanities and social sciences ordinarily resident in the UK, holding a current long-term appointment at a UK-based Higher Education Institution (HEI) or Independent Research Organisation (IRO) continuing for the full duration of the award, intending to pursue original independent research in the humanities or social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Awards to promote the acquisition and advancement of skills in relevant areas by UK-based researchers, supporting innovative research methods through skills development (e.g. quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities, languages), collaboration or dissemination.

opportunities.title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and The British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027

amount.raw: The symposium covers travel, accommodation, and visa costs

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early career researchers in the humanities and social sciences affiliated with research institutions in the UK or Germany.
opportunities.summary: Call for early career researchers in the humanities and social sciences to attend a research collaboration symposium on the theme 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future', in partnership with The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, bringing together around fifteen early career researchers from the UK and fifteen from Germany.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027

amount.raw: Up to £300,000 over 2 years at 80% FEC (total project value at 100% FEC may not exceed £375,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Principal Investigator must be a researcher from the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research institute, holding an established role lasting at least the duration of the award, of postdoctoral status or above, planning to spend at least 20% time on the award. Involvement of overseas Co-Applicants is required, with collaboration across disciplines.
opportunities.summary: International interdisciplinary research projects led by UK-based researchers in the humanities and social sciences, working with international partners, on the theme of Mobilities, ranging across all SHAPE and STEM disciplines.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27

amount.raw: Up to £150,000 for 12 months (with Full Economic Costing at 80 per cent)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK-based early- and mid-career researchers from across the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Up to two one-year fellowships offering UK-based early- and mid-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences the opportunity to embed themselves in the office of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) in Berlin, developing skills, networks and careers in policy sectors.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs

amount.raw: up to £4,000 (exceptional circumstances may consider above £4,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Available to current British Academy award-holders on any scheme OR applicants intending to apply for a British Academy award in the next six months. If not a current award-holder, must identify the scheme they intend to apply for and meet its eligibility requirements.
opportunities.summary: Funding to support additional needs that applicants and award-holders may require (e.g. specific equipment to overcome barriers, assistance for sensory impairment, caring costs for research trips, support in making an application), additional to the amount already requested for research expenses. Reviewed on a rolling, case-by-case basis.
